experiments.attack: Deliver a pull_request webhook signed with a wrong secret, a correctly signed body altered after signing, and an unsigned body
experiments.consequence: An attacker without the webhook secret cannot trigger or suppress scans
experiments.expected: All rejected before parsing; no scan, no check
experiments.limitation: A leaked webhook secret defeats this control; rotate it
experiments.mitigation: HMAC-SHA256 signature verified in constant time over the raw body
experiments.observed: HTTP 401 (wrong secret), 401 (altered body), 401 (unsigned), reasons ["{'error': 'invalid webhook signature'}", "{'error': 'invalid webhook signature'}", "{'error': 'missing webhook signature'}"]; scans processed 0; check runs before the control 0; correctly signed control: {'status': 'queued'}

experiments.attack: Redeliver an old webhook (same delivery ID), then deliver the old event again under a new delivery ID after a newer commit was scanned
experiments.consequence: A PASS for an outdated commit cannot hide a violation added later
experiments.expected: The replay is a duplicate; the late event cannot turn the pull request's newer BLOCK into a PASS
experiments.limitation: Checks are per commit SHA: an old commit's own check can still show its old result, which is correct for that SHA
experiments.mitigation: Delivery records with payload digests; check ownership per repository, SHA and check name; newest-scan-wins
experiments.observed: replay response {'status': 'duplicate'}; late event response {'status': 'duplicate'}; newest commit check still failure; old commit job states ['passed']

experiments.attack: GitHub's API is unreachable during a scan of a clean commit; separately, the installation's Checks permission is reduced to read
experiments.consequence: A required check stays unsatisfied; merges wait instead of passing unverified code
experiments.expected: Neither produces a successful check (fail closed)
experiments.limitation: Availability: while GitHub or the service is down, required checks block merging
experiments.mitigation: Bounded retries, then ERROR; never a success conclusion without a completed evaluation
experiments.observed: outage: job error (infrastructure), check conclusions []; revoked: job error (authorization), check runs 0

experiments.attack: Re-run the passing check of an outdated commit after a violating commit was pushed; queue a pull request whose own head passed while an AI-attributed change is queued ahead of it
experiments.consequence: Neither a stale re-run nor a queue candidate can inherit an earlier PASS
experiments.expected: The stale re-run is refused; the merge group commit is scanned itself and blocked
experiments.limitation: Requires the repository's merge queue to require the CommitGuard check
experiments.mitigation: Re-runs only for the newest commit of a pull request or branch; merge_group events scan base..merge-group SHA
experiments.observed: stale re-run response {'status': 'ignored'}; newest pull request check failure; pull request head check success; merge group 268db8c11243 check failure

experiments.consequence: Repository administrators cannot opt out of organization requirements
experiments.expected: Without a central floor the repository decides; with a mandatory policy the rule still blocks
experiments.limitation: Only repositories scanned by the GitHub App with the floor configured are covered; GitHub Actions uses repository configuration
experiments.mitigation: Mandatory policy floors (service policy, Phase 8 organization/group mandatory entries)
experiments.observed: without mandatory policy: success; with mandatory policy: failure

experiments.attack: The service database fails while a webhook is received
experiments.consequence: No false PASS; the event is not lost if GitHub redelivers it
experiments.expected: The webhook is answered with an error (so GitHub can redeliver); no check is reported as passing; a redelivery after recovery is processed
experiments.limitation: GitHub does not redeliver automatically: an operator must redeliver from the App's delivery log
experiments.mitigation: Event recorded before processing; errors surface as 5xx; redelivery processed
experiments.observed: HTTP 500 {"error": "internal error"}; scans processed 0; checks while down []; redelivery response {'status': 'queued'}; check after recovery success

experiments.attack: The GitHub App installation is suspended, then a pull request is opened
experiments.consequence: Enforcement stops while suspended and the dashboard shows repositories at risk instead of protected
experiments.expected: State recorded, audit event and notification created, no passing check
experiments.limitation: While suspended GitHub sends no events and no check is created; only a required check keeps merges blocked
experiments.mitigation: Installation lifecycle events, critical notification, AT RISK posture
experiments.observed: installation state suspended; scans processed 0; checks []; audit contains installation_suspended: True; notification installation_disconnected: True

experiments.attack: git commit --no-verify and git push --no-verify with an AI co-author trailer
experiments.consequence: The violating commit reaches the remote branch but cannot be merged while the check is required
experiments.expected: Local hooks are skipped; the pull request check blocks the commit
experiments.limitation: Without a required check, a --no-verify push can be merged; CommitGuard cannot configure branch protection
experiments.mitigation: Server-side check (GitHub Actions or GitHub App) required by branch protection or a ruleset
experiments.observed: normal commit exit 1; --no-verify commit exit 0; --no-verify push exit 0; pull request check exit 1 (BLOCK); modelled required-check gate allows merge: False

experiments.attack: Delete the pre-commit, commit-msg and pre-push hook files, then commit and push
experiments.consequence: Local prevention is lost silently until doctor is run
experiments.expected: Local enforcement is gone; doctor reports it; the pull request check blocks
experiments.limitation: Git gives hooks no integrity protection; a developer controls their own .git/hooks
experiments.observed: commit exit 0 (allowed); doctor exit 2, reports missing hooks: True; pull request check exit 1 (BLOCK)

experiments.attack: Edit the managed hook block so it exits 0 before running CommitGuard
experiments.consequence: Local prevention silently disabled for this clone
experiments.expected: The edited hook allows the commit; doctor flags the checksum mismatch; the pull request check blocks
experiments.limitation: A checksum detects edits only when doctor runs; it does not prevent them
experiments.mitigation: Managed-block checksum reported by commitguard doctor; server-side required check
experiments.observed: commit exit 0; doctor reports modified hooks: True; pull request check exit 1 (BLOCK)

experiments.attack: Point core.hooksPath at an empty directory; separately, commit from a fresh clone without installing hooks
experiments.consequence: Any clone without CommitGuard hooks has no local enforcement
experiments.expected: Both commits are allowed locally; both pull request checks block
experiments.limitation: Hooks are per clone and opt-in by design of Git
experiments.mitigation: Server-side required check; commitguard install --global for developer machines
experiments.observed: core.hooksPath commit exit 0; fresh clone commit exit 0; pull request checks exit 1 and 1

experiments.attack: In the pull request itself, disable ai_coauthor, set it to allow, or delete .commitguard.yaml
experiments.consequence: A pull request cannot relax the policy that evaluates it
experiments.expected: Policy is read from the pull request base; every variant is blocked
experiments.limitation: Once a relaxing change is merged into the base branch it applies to later pull requests, unless an organization mandatory policy (GitHub App) sets a floor
experiments.mitigation: Trusted policy source: the base commit (Phase 4)
experiments.observed: pull request check exit codes: disable=1, allow=1, delete=1

experiments.attack: A pull request removes or neuters the CommitGuard workflow so no check runs
experiments.consequence: Only branch protection that requires the check stops the merge; the GitHub App check does not depend on the repository's workflow files
experiments.expected: No successful required check exists, so a required-check gate refuses the merge
experiments.limitation: Modelled gate, not GitHub: verifying the real branch protection needs a GitHub repository (see docs/research/github-enforcement-validation.md)
experiments.mitigation: Require the check in branch protection or a ruleset; prefer the GitHub App, which runs outside the repository
experiments.observed: no check conclusion for c61279998f75; modelled gate allows merge: False

notes: Each hook starts a Python interpreter; interpreter start-up is part of the measured overhead.
Pushes go to a local bare repository, so network latency is excluded.
--no-verify results demonstrate that local hooks are advisory; server-side enforcement is measured separately.
